 Micron Stocks Rise 3.41% as $1,700 Target Puts Cash Durability in Focus
 Less than 1 min read MU Memory producer Micron MU rose 3.41% to $885.685 at 11.30 a.m. ET on October 23, as investors weighed BNP Paribas's $1,700 price target. According to Barron's, analyst Karl Ackerman maintained his Buy rating and highlighted memory constraints in AI inference. That target implies roughly 91.9% upside. The hurdle is clear: Micron needs to keep turning tight supply into cash. 
 The cash engine is already running hard. Micron reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $54.23 billion and operating cash flow of $43.97 billion. Net capital investment consumed $10.77 billion, leaving adjusted free cash flow of $33.20 billionabout 61.2% of revenue. Those numbers give the bullish case substance. Keeping that cash conversion strong as investment climbs is the next test. 
 The valuation picture adds a reality check: shares trade 11.04% above the $797.62 GF Value estimate, suggesting some optimism is already priced in. AI demand can keep memory shipments growing, but more capacity could pressure pricing. Watch selling prices, shipment growth and capital spending together. One exceptional quarter supports the story; sustained cash generation has to carry the valuation.
